unit.title: Shortest and best: puzzles, paths, packing

lesson.title: Pack the truck
lesson.subtitle: A rule, a goal, and the best load

video.title: Pack the truck
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — your teacher (main character)
Mr Okafor Eze — your science teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, talks to the student)

scenes.visual: Amina beside a small truck at the school gate, with a pile of boxes far too big for it.
scenes.animation: Boxes pile up higher than the truck; Amina scratches her head.
scenes.narration: A truck is bringing supplies to our village school. It can carry a thousand kilos, but the school needs more than that. So what should go on the truck?

scenes.visual: Title card with the Darsi mark and the Optimization track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: pack the truck, and find the best load.

scenes.visual: Two big cards: a scale with a red line at 1,000 kg, and a star with points.
scenes.animation: The scale tips; the star sparkles.
scenes.narration: Every packing puzzle has a rule and a goal. The rule: no more than a thousand kilos. The goal: the most points, because points show how much the school needs each thing.

scenes.visual: Six loads in a row, each with its weight and points on a tag.
scenes.animation: Tags flip over one by one.
scenes.narration: Solar panels weigh six hundred kilos, and give forty-two points. Desks and books weigh five hundred each. They give thirty-three and thirty-two points. Then there’s a water filter, footballs, and chalk and paper.

scenes.visual: The solar panels go on the truck, then the filter, then the chalk; the weight bar fills to 1,000.
scenes.animation: Loads slide onto the truck; the points count up to 60.
scenes.narration: Here’s a quick way. First, load the thing with the most points for its weight: the solar panels. Then only the water filter and the chalk still fit. That’s sixty points.

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor points at the truck with the solar panels on it. Three answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Quick check! The solar panels are on the truck: six hundred kilos. Can the desks, five hundred kilos, go on too?

scenes.visual: The scale needle goes past the red line; a big red cross appears.
scenes.animation: The needle swings into the red; the cross stamps down.
scenes.narration: No: six hundred and five hundred make eleven hundred. That’s too heavy. A load that breaks the rule doesn’t count, however many points it has.

scenes.visual: Two columns: the quick way (60 points) and desks with books (65 points).
scenes.animation: The right column glows; a star pops.
scenes.narration: Now try the desks and the books. Five hundred and five hundred make exactly a thousand. And thirty-three and thirty-two make sixty-five points, more than sixty!

scenes.visual: A grid of 64 tiny trucks; one glows gold.
scenes.animation: Trucks appear in rows; the gold one pulses.
scenes.narration: So the quick way wasn’t the best. The best load has the most points and still keeps the rule. With six loads, there are sixty-four ways to pack, so you can check them all.

scenes.visual: The solar panels wait at the warehouse door as the truck drives away; a calendar shows next week.
scenes.animation: The truck drives off; the calendar page turns.
scenes.narration: Something always stays behind. This time, it’s the solar panels. Who decides? Could they come on the next trip?

scenes.visual: A phone with the lab: six load tiles, a truck and a weight bar.
scenes.animation: A finger taps tiles; the weight bar fills.
scenes.narration: In the app, tap loads to put them on the truck yourself. Watch the weight, and count your points. Then press Show the best load, and compare.

scenes.visual: Amina holds a tablet showing a truck with desks and a filter. Three answer cards appear.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Your load is the desks and the water filter: eight hundred kilos and forty-eight points. Is it the best load?

scenes.visual: Summary lines and an orange takeaway bar.
scenes.animation: Lines tick in; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: No: it keeps the rule, but the desks and the books give sixty-five. Remember: keep the rule first, then chase the goal. Quick ways are good, but check them. And think about what stays behind.

scenes.visual: A pupil’s desk: a school bag, books, a water bottle and a lunch box, each with a paper tag.
scenes.animation: Things hop into the bag; a friend gives a thumbs up.
scenes.narration: Try it yourself: pack your school bag like a truck. Give each thing a weight and points, and choose a limit. Find the load with the most points, then ask a friend to beat it.

checkpoints.prompt: The solar panels (600 kg) are on. Can the desks (500 kg) go on too?

options.text: Only if we take off the chalk

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — 600 + 500 = 1,100 kg, more than the truck can carry.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — add them up: 600 + 500 = 1,100 kg. That’s more than 1,000, so the desks don’t fit.

checkpoints.prompt: Desks and the water filter: 800 kg and 48 points. Is it the best load?

options.text: No: desks and books give more points

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — it keeps the rule, but desks and books give 65 points.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — it fits (800 kg), but it isn’t the best: desks and books weigh 1,000 kg and give 65 points.
